description.en-US: The bill this money settles. Immutable: a payment is measured against a bill's total, and moving one between bills would change what both are owed.
The paymentinvoice payment method used. A plain ulid with no edge: payment methods belong to another module, and a foreign key across that boundary would make the two modules undeployable apart.

The method's code AS IT WAS when the payment was taken. Snapshotted because a receipt printed last year must still say how the customer paid, even after the method has been renamed or withdrawn - the same reasoning as the product snapshots on an order line.
How much was taken. Positive: a refund is a separate record with its own resource (SALES-035), not a negative payment, because the two have different lifecycles and different approval rules.
The currency taken, copied from the bill. Sales has no FX, so a payment in a currency the bill does not use cannot be reconciled against it and is refused rather than converted.

Where this payment stands with the provider. Only 'captured' counts toward settling the bill: an authorization is a hold the provider may still release, and treating it as money in would settle a bill against funds that never arrived.

The provider's own identifier for this transaction. Unique per bill when present, and that index IS the dedupe mechanism (D-29): a gateway callback that arrives twice must not record the money twice, and a check-then-insert can be raced by the retry it is meant to catch. Null for a cash payment, which no provider issued an id for.

Whatever else the provider returned that identifies this payment on their side - an authorization code, a terminal reference. Kept for reconciliation and dispute handling; unlike external_transaction_id it is not required to be unique and carries no rule.

The paymentinvoice order this payment is being collected through, for a gateway tender. A plain string with no edge, like payment_method_id: the order belongs to another module, and a foreign key across that boundary would make the two modules undeployable apart. Null for cash, which no gateway ever saw. It is the correlation key a settlement arrives on, so it is written when the order is opened and never changed.

When the money was captured. Null while the payment is still pending or authorized; set once and never cleared, because a captured payment that later fails is a refund or a chargeback rather than an un-capture.
